limitations: Operationally heavy to self-host and not meant as a desktop tool; two older repos in this lineage are archived or dormant, so older tutorials point at dead code.

name: OONI Data (oonidata / oonipipeline)
maintainer: Open Observatory of Network Interference (OONI) Foundation ETS
description: CLI and 'Pipeline v5' for working with OONI measurement data in bulk - syncing raw measurements, re-processing them into analysis-ready observations, and running blocking-detection logic outside OONI's own infrastructure.
journalism_use_case: The tool to reach for when a story needs a country-wide or multi-year blocking dataset rather than individual measurements, e.g. reconstructing exactly when a set of news domains started being tampered with.
deployment: self-hosted CLI and pipeline (Docker configs and Airflow-style DAGs present in-repo)
activity_evidence: GitHub API: pushed_at 2026-11-16; 11 stars; archived=false; homepage https://docs.ooni.org/data. Root tree contains oonidata/, oonipipeline/, dags/, notebooks/.
platform_api_risk: Depends on OONI's bulk data stores and API staying accessible and schema-stable; pipeline generations (v3/v4/v5) have broken compatibility before.
external_deps: OONI measurement archive (bulk object storage), ClickHouse-class analytics store for the pipeline, Python 3 toolchain.
data_flows: Pulls already-public OONI measurements down to local or cloud storage and derives observation tables; no new measurement traffic is generated.
limitations: GitHub reports no licence for this repo because the root has no LICENSE file - the BSD-3-Clause text sits in the oonidata/ and oonipipeline/ subpackages, so licence clarity at the repo level is poor. Full-corpus processing needs real storage and compute; analyst tooling, not a newsroom app.

name: OONI Explorer
maintainer: Open Observatory of Network Interference (OONI) Foundation ETS
description: Open-source web front end over OONI's measurement archive that lets anyone browse per-country, per-network and per-URL blocking evidence, inspect individual raw measurements, and link to a permanent URL for each one.
journalism_use_case: The fastest route from 'is this site blocked in country X' to a citable, linkable public measurement; the per-measurement permalinks are usable directly as sourcing in a published story.
deployment: hosted public service at explorer.ooni.org; self-hostable from source
activity_evidence: GitHub API: pushed_at 2026-11-16; 95 stars; archived=false. Hosted instance https://explorer.ooni.org returned HTTP 200 when checked on 2026-11-16.
platform_api_risk: Depends entirely on the OONI measurements API (api.ooni.io) remaining available; a self-hosted copy is not useful without that backend or your own pipeline.
external_deps: OONI backend/measurements API; OONI's published measurement data store.
data_flows: Reads and displays already-public OONI measurement data; browsing is read-only and no measurement is run from the browser.
limitations: Shows anomalies and confirmed-blocking classifications, not a verdict on who ordered a block; low-coverage countries and networks can look quiet simply because nobody ran a probe there.

name: OONI Probe CLI / probe-engine
maintainer: Open Observatory of Network Interference (OONI) Foundation ETS
description: Go command-line client and measurement engine that runs OONI's censorship nettests (Web Connectivity, DNS consistency, HTTP invalid request line, Signal/Telegram/WhatsApp/Facebook Messenger reachability, Tor and Psiphon reachability) from a vantage point inside a network and submits results to OONI's open collector.
journalism_use_case: A reporter or local stringer runs ooniprobe from inside the affected country to generate timestamped, independently published evidence that specific news sites or messaging apps are being blocked, and what technique is doing the blocking.
deployment: self-hosted / local binary (Linux, macOS, Windows); also embedded as the engine in OONI's desktop and mobile apps
activity_evidence: GitHub API: pushed_at 2026-11-16; releases v3.31.1 published 2026-11-03 and v3.31.0 on 2026-10-22; 300 stars; archived=false. Companion ooni/probe-engine (GPL-3.0) pushed 2026-10-22.
platform_api_risk: Nettests target third-party platforms (Telegram, Signal, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger), so endpoint or protocol changes by those vendors can cause false positives until a test is updated.
external_deps: OONI backend collector and test-helper infrastructure; Citizen Lab URL test lists; MaxMind-style GeoIP databases for ASN/country tagging.
data_flows: Measurement results are uploaded by default to OONI's collector and then published as open data, including the probe's ASN, country code, and network name; OONI documents that IP addresses are not intentionally published but measurement data is public by design.
limitations: Running probes is legally and physically risky for the operator in repressive jurisdictions; results detect anomalies, not intent, and confirming blocking usually needs corroboration across probes and time; no built-in anonymity for the person running it.

name: OONI Probe Multiplatform (Android / iOS / Desktop)
maintainer: Open Observatory of Network Interference (OONI) Foundation ETS
description: Kotlin Multiplatform rewrite of the OONI Probe end-user app for Android, iOS and desktop, giving non-technical users a tap-to-run interface over the same measurement engine used by the CLI.
journalism_use_case: Newsrooms can ask sources, correspondents or volunteer networks inside a country to install one app and run a standard test suite, producing comparable public measurements without any command-line skills.
deployment: end-user mobile and desktop app; built from source or installed from app stores
activity_evidence: GitHub API: pushed_at 2026-11-16; releases v6.3.1 published 2026-11-09, v6.3.0 on 2026-11-02, v6.2.1 on 2026-09-28; 99 stars; archived=false. Supersedes the legacy Java app ooni/probe-android, which the API reports as archived=true (pushed_at 2026-04-20).
platform_api_risk: App-store distribution is a real chokepoint: store availability in censored markets is outside OONI's control, and messaging-app nettests break when vendors change endpoints.
external_deps: OONI probe engine (Go, from probe-cli); OONI backend collector; Citizen Lab test lists; Google Play / Apple App Store for mainstream distribution.
data_flows: Results upload to OONI's collector and are republished as open data with ASN, network name and country; the app surfaces consent screens about this public publication before testing.
limitations: Still an app the user must deliberately install and run, so coverage is opportunistic and biased toward activist and technical populations; the older Android codebase is archived, so bug reports must go to the new repo.

name: PyBGPStream / libbgpstream
maintainer: CAIDA, UC San Diego; actively forked and maintained by Georgia Tech's Internet Intelligence Lab
description: C library and Python bindings for streaming and analysing historical and live BGP routing data from RouteViews, RIPE RIS and similar collectors, including route withdrawals and prefix visibility over time.
journalism_use_case: Lets a data journalist independently reconstruct which ASNs withdrew which prefixes, and at what minute, during a shutdown - the evidence that distinguishes an operator-executed disconnection from a transit failure.
deployment: self-hosted library; pulls data from public BGP collector archives
activity_evidence: GitHub API: CAIDA/pybgpstream pushed_at 2026-07-06, 45 stars, archived=false, latest release v2.0.4 published 2024-02-20. The C client library has moved forward under InetIntel/libbgpstream (BSD-2-Clause, pushed_at 2026-07-07); CAIDA/bgpstream itself is dormant (pushed_at 2019-12-19).
platform_api_risk: Entirely dependent on third-party BGP collector archives (RouteViews, RIPE RIS) remaining public and on their file formats; broker endpoints have changed between versions.
external_deps: libbgpstream and its C build chain (wandio, librdkafka), RouteViews/RIPE RIS MRT archives.
data_flows: Reads public routing-table and update archives; no probing and no user data.
limitations: Build and dependency setup is genuinely fiddly and release cadence is slow (last tagged release 2024); BGP shows control-plane intent, so routes can stay announced while the data plane is blocked, and vice versa. Maintenance is split between the CAIDA and InetIntel lineages, a confusing provenance picture.

name: pywb
description: Core Python web archiving toolkit for recording and, above all, replaying web archives - it serves WARC/WACZ collections as a browsable Wayback-style interface and can proxy-record new captures.
journalism_use_case: Stand up a private Wayback Machine over your own captures so editors and lawyers can click through dated versions of a government page side by side without relying on a public archive staying online.
language_stack: Python; WARC/CDXJ indexes; Docker images available
deployment: self-hosted server (wayback CLI / Docker), typically fronting a collection of WARC or WACZ files
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-16T07:47:24Z, GPL-3.0 confirmed via licence endpoint (LICENSE at main), 1,720 stars, 189 open issues, not archived.
platform_api_risk: None inherent; it replays archives you hold.
external_deps: Python 3; WARC/WACZ inputs from crawlers such as browsertrix-crawler, Heritrix, wget or warcprox
data_flows: Serves local archive files; what it exposes to the network depends entirely on how you deploy it.
limitations: Replay and recording only - no change detection, diffing or alerting; replay fidelity for heavily scripted modern pages remains an open problem in web archiving generally; GPL-3.0 copyleft.

name: RIPE Atlas tooling (Magellan CLI, Cousteau, Sagan)
description: Official RIPE Atlas client suite: the ripe-atlas command-line tool (Magellan) for creating and streaming measurements, Cousteau as the Python API client, and Sagan as the result-parsing library, driving a global fleet of thousands of hardware and software probes.
journalism_use_case: Lets a reporter schedule pings, traceroutes, DNS and TLS measurements from probes inside a specific country or ASN during an unfolding shutdown, and watch probe disconnections as an independent outage signal.
deployment: local CLI/library against the hosted RIPE Atlas API and probe network
activity_evidence: GitHub API: ripe-atlas-tools pushed_at 2026-10-22, 218 stars, archived=false, latest release v3.2.0 published 2025-09-25; ripe-atlas-cousteau pushed_at 2026-10-22 (GPL-3.0, 68 stars, last release v2.0.0 on 2023-01-20); ripe-atlas-sagan pushed_at 2026-06-03 (GPL-3.0, 52 stars).
platform_api_risk: Significant: creating measurements requires a RIPE Atlas API key and spends 'credits' earned by hosting a probe, and RIPE NCC controls quotas, fair-use rules and probe availability. Terms changes directly affect what a newsroom can run.
external_deps: RIPE Atlas REST API and credit system; the volunteer-hosted probe fleet; Python 3 environment.
data_flows: Measurements are initiated by you from third-party probes and, by default, results are published publicly in RIPE Atlas; probe hosts' approximate locations and ASNs are public.
limitations: Probe coverage is thin and skewed in exactly the countries that matter most for shutdown reporting, so a country may have too few probes to say anything; credits are a real throttle on sustained measurement, and an absent probe is not evidence of an outage. Cousteau's last tagged release is from 2023.

name: Scoop
description: Browser-based single-page web archiving library and CLI, described by its maintainers as built for 'witnessing the web' - it captures one page at high fidelity with an emphasis on provenance and verifiable capture records. From the lab behind Perma.cc.
journalism_use_case: Capture a single official page at the moment you read it, with provenance metadata attached, so the capture stands up later as evidence of what the page said before a quiet edit.
language_stack: JavaScript/Node.js with a headless browser; WARC/WACZ output
deployment: self-hosted CLI or embedded as a Node library
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-09-25T16:00:00Z, MIT confirmed via licence endpoint (LICENSE at main), 217 stars, not archived. Sibling harvard-lil/perma pushed 2026-11-03, licence not returned by GitHub metadata.
platform_api_risk: Low; it drives a local browser. Capabilities such as attested/signed captures depend on the surrounding toolchain rather than a vendor API.
external_deps: Node.js, a Chromium-family browser, WARC/WACZ tooling; replay needs ReplayWeb.page or pywb
data_flows: Captures written locally to files you control; no third-party submission by default.
limitations: Single-page scope by design - no crawling, scheduling, diffing or alerting; detailed signing/provenance formats were not individually verified beyond the maintainers' description.

name: shot-scraper
description: CLI that uses Playwright to take scripted screenshots of web pages and to scrape them with JavaScript, driven by a YAML file of shots. It is the capture half of the 'git scraping' pattern, where scheduled runs commit outputs to a Git repository so the commit history becomes the change log.
journalism_use_case: Run a scheduled job that screenshots or extracts a government page and commits the result to Git, turning every quiet edit into a dated, diffable commit you can point at in a story.
language_stack: Python + Playwright/Chromium; YAML shot definitions; pairs with git-history (Apache-2.0) and Datasette (Apache-2.0)
deployment: local CLI or scheduled CI runner (commonly GitHub Actions on a cron)
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: shot-scraper pushed_at 2026-10-14T03:21:49Z, Apache-2.0 confirmed via licence endpoint, 2,608 stars, not archived. Companions same day: simonw/git-history pushed 2025-12-21 (Apache-2.0), simonw/datasette pushed 2026-11-16 (Apache-2.0).
platform_api_risk: Depends on Playwright/Chromium upgrades; if run in CI, on that provider's scheduling and runner policies (GitHub Actions cron reliability and usage limits).
external_deps: Python 3, Playwright browsers; optional GitHub Actions or other scheduler; optional git-history/Datasette for querying the resulting history
data_flows: Outputs land in your repository or local disk; if the repo is public, the monitored URLs and captured content become public too.
limitations: No notification or diff-review layer - you assemble alerting yourself from Git tooling or CI; requires comfort with YAML, Git and CI; screenshots alone are not text-diffable, so pair with JS/text extraction.

name: urlwatch
description: Long-running command-line tool that watches URLs (and shell command output) defined in a YAML jobs file, applies filters to strip boilerplate, and reports unified diffs through pluggable reporters. It is the ancestor of several later monitoring tools.
journalism_use_case: Script a reproducible watchlist of statute, regulation or guidance pages in version control, and receive diffs by email, Slack, Matrix or stdout when an official page is edited.
deployment: self-hosted / local CLI, usually driven by cron or systemd timers
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-07-10T08:56:34Z, 3,148 stars, 85 open issues, not archived; HEAD commits dated 2026-07-09/10. The releases/latest endpoint returned 404, so release cadence was not confirmed.
platform_api_risk: Low; plain HTTP fetching plus optional Playwright 'browser' jobs, so JS rendering depends on the browser stack rather than any vendor API.
external_deps: Python 3; optional Playwright for browser jobs; optional jq/html2text/beautifulsoup-style filters; reporter-specific credentials
data_flows: Snapshot cache and diffs stay on the local machine; only the configured reporter transmits content off-box.
limitations: CLI/text-first with no web UI or multi-user triage; no built-in archiving of the captured snapshot as evidence; four-month gap since last push at time of checking.

name: wayback (Python client for the Internet Archive Wayback Machine)
description: Python API client for the Internet Archive Wayback Machine that searches CDX capture indexes and retrieves the raw archived content of specific mementos, built and maintained by EDGI for its government-website monitoring pipeline.
journalism_use_case: Enumerate every archived capture of a government URL and pull the exact bytes of two dates to prove what a page said before and after an edit, without screen-scraping the Wayback web interface.
deployment: library installed via pip into your own scripts or pipeline
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-06T21:30:02Z, BSD-3-Clause confirmed via the licence endpoint (LICENSE at main), 94 stars, not archived.
platform_api_risk: High dependency on Internet Archive services: the CDX/memento endpoints are undocumented-to-semi-documented, rate limited, occasionally unavailable, and subject to IA's terms and exclusion policies, all of which can break or blank out a monitoring run.
external_deps: Internet Archive Wayback Machine CDX and memento endpoints; Python 3; requests-style HTTP stack
data_flows: Sends the URLs you query to the Internet Archive and pulls archived content back; your query pattern is visible to IA.
limitations: Only as good as IA's crawl coverage - pages never captured, captured rarely, or excluded cannot be reconstructed; no diffing, scheduling or alerting of its own.

name: webchanges
description: Actively maintained Python tool, derived from urlwatch, that checks web content (including PDFs, images and command output) for changes and reports rich HTML diffs, with optional AI-generated change summaries.
journalism_use_case: Monitor official documents and dashboards that urlwatch handles poorly (PDF text, images, JSON APIs) and receive readable HTML diffs of what an agency altered.
deployment: self-hosted / local CLI via pip, scheduled by cron or Task Scheduler
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: pushed_at 2026-11-15T08:26:43Z, 50 stars, 6 open issues, not archived. LICENSE.md read 2026-11-16 states 'The MIT License (MIT) Copyright (c) 2020- Mike Borsetti' plus a redistribution notice for urlwatch 2.21 under BSD-3-Clause terms.
platform_api_risk: Optional AI summarisation sends page content to an external LLM provider, which is a configuration-time choice; otherwise plain HTTP plus optional Playwright.
external_deps: Python 3; optional Playwright/Chromium; optional LLM API key for AI summaries; reporter credentials
data_flows: Snapshots and diffs held locally; content leaves the machine only via configured reporters or, if enabled, the AI summarisation provider.
limitations: Effectively a single-maintainer project with a small user base; no web UI or collaborative review; the AI summary feature introduces a third-party data-sharing decision newsrooms should review before use on sensitive beats.

name: 4get
description: Self-hostable proxy metasearch engine in PHP that scrapes and reformats results from multiple upstream engines, including images and video.

activity_evidence: Most recent commit shown 2026-11-15 19:41 ('forgot settings woopsies', 4c7c4ea072) on git.lolcat.ca; licence stated as AGPLv3-only

external_deps: Upstream search engines; PHP runtime

name: ArchiveBot
description: IRC-driven bot infrastructure that coordinates volunteer archiving of websites into WARC collections.

name: ArchiveWeb.page
description: Chrome/Chromium extension that records high-fidelity web archives of pages as you browse them, exporting WACZ/WARC.
journalism_use_case: Manually capture a social post, story or logged-in page exactly as seen, producing a replayable file for the evidence locker.

name: Browsertrix

name: browsertrix-behaviors

name: brozzler

name: Conifer

name: Exiv2
description: C++ library and CLI to read and write image metadata including EXIF, IPTC, XMP and ICC profiles, used as the metadata engine inside many other applications.
journalism_use_case: Embed metadata extraction into a newsroom ingest pipeline so every incoming image is automatically parsed for timestamps and GPS before an analyst sees it.
data_licence_terms: No external data service; local file processing only.
deployment: system library plus CLI; bundled in digiKam, KDE and other tools
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2026-11-09, 1172 stars, not archived. LICENSE.txt states GPL version 2 or (at your option) any later version.
external_deps: C++ toolchain; optional zlib/expat. No API keys, no GPU.
data_flows: Entirely local.
limitations: Same fundamental caveat as all metadata tools: metadata is writer-controlled and routinely stripped, so it corroborates rather than proves. Engineer-facing, not an analyst UI.

name: imagededup
description: Python package for finding exact and near-duplicate images using multiple hashing methods plus CNN embeddings, with built-in evaluation of deduplication quality.
journalism_use_case: Deduplicate a large scraped image corpus before manual review, collapsing thousands of reposts into unique images so analyst time goes to genuinely new material.
data_licence_terms: No data service. CNN method downloads pretrained ImageNet weights with their own upstream terms.
deployment: pip install imagededup
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2025-08-15, 5685 stars, not archived. Roughly 15 months without commits.
external_deps: Python; deep-learning runtime for the CNN method; GPU optional and only helpful for CNN embeddings.
data_flows: Local processing; model weights fetched once.
limitations: Duplicate groupings are similarity judgements requiring a tuned threshold; CNN embeddings cluster semantically similar but distinct images, which is wrong for forensic identity. Development has slowed.

name: Katna
description: Python library automating keyframe extraction from video and smart cropping of images, selecting frames by clustering on colour histograms plus blur and brightness filtering.
journalism_use_case: Automatically pick the most informative, least blurry frames from shaky phone footage to use as geolocation and reverse-image-search candidates.
data_licence_terms: No data service; local media only.
deployment: pip install katna
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2024-08-06, 401 stars, not archived. About two years without commits.
external_deps: Python, OpenCV, FFmpeg. No API keys, no GPU.
data_flows: Entirely local.
limitations: Frame selection is optimised for visual appeal and diversity, not evidential completeness, so it can discard the one frame that matters; always verify against the full video. Maintenance has stalled and dependency pinning is dated.

name: pHash
description: The original perceptual hash C++ library computing robust fingerprints for images, audio and video, with DCT, radial and MH hash variants.
journalism_use_case: Match a short audio or video clip against a reference library to identify re-used broadcast or propaganda material, where image-only hashing is insufficient.
data_licence_terms: No data service; local media only.
deployment: build from source as a C++ library
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2026-06-09, 664 stars, not archived.
external_deps: C++ toolchain, CImg, FFmpeg for video/audio. No API keys, no GPU.
data_flows: Entirely local.
limitations: GPL-3.0 copyleft constrains embedding in closed newsroom products. Low-level library with sparse modern documentation; audio/video hashing needs careful parameterisation. Matches are similarity signals, not proof.

name: ThreatExchange (PDQ / TMK+PDQF / vPDQ)
description: Meta's open-sourced content-matching toolkit: the PDQ photo hash, TMK+PDQF and vPDQ video hashes, reference implementations and the Hasher-Matcher-Actioner matching service.
journalism_use_case: Index known footage (e.g. frames from a verified incident video) and match at scale against newly collected social uploads to trace how a clip spreads and spot re-uploads with altered captions.
data_licence_terms: Software is BSD-3-Clause. The separate Meta ThreatExchange hash-sharing PLATFORM requires an approved partner account under its own terms; the open algorithms do not. No imagery bundled.
deployment: local libraries/CLIs; HMA deployable via Docker/AWS
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2026-11-09, 1411 stars, not archived. GitHub reported NOASSERTION; LICENSE file is a BSD licence for ThreatExchange software, Meta Platforms copyright.
external_deps: Per-language toolchains; container/cloud infra for HMA. No GPU for PDQ.
data_flows: Hashing is local. If connected to Meta's platform, hashes (not images) are exchanged under partner terms.
limitations: A hash match is a strong similarity signal, not proof of provenance or authenticity; video hashing degrades under re-encoding and editing. Designed for matching known content, not discovering manipulation.

name: VFRAME
description: Computer-vision toolkit built for human-rights research on large video and image archives, with pipelines for object detection (including custom munitions detectors), frame extraction, redaction and metadata handling.
journalism_use_case: Triage very large conflict-footage archives by flagging frames likely to contain a specific object, such as a cluster-munition remnant, so investigators review a shortlist instead of thousands of hours.
data_licence_terms: No bundled data service. Custom detector models and training datasets are distributed separately with their own terms; source footage rights stay with the archive owner.
deployment: local CLI; GPU recommended
activity_evidence: GitHub API 2026-11-16: last push 2023-05-28, 76 stars, not archived. Dormant for roughly three and a half years.
external_deps: Python, OpenCV, deep-learning runtime; NVIDIA GPU strongly recommended. No paid API.
data_flows: Local processing of local archives.
limitations: Detector outputs are probabilistic signals requiring human confirmation of every hit, never conclusive identification. Long dormancy means dependency rot is likely. Custom models are domain-specific and degrade on unfamiliar footage.
